body:
TRUST-ROOT (touches a rails deny-path, so a distinct-provider cross-model approve is required before merge).

The always-on handoff artifact guard — the deny-set protection that refuses writes to `.adlc/handoffs/denies/**`, `.adlc/.deny-store`, resume-auth caches, model-ok stamps, and lock files whether or not a deny is active — extracts its candidate paths from tool arguments with extractors that only see SOME of the shapes those arguments arrive in.

Found while fixing the rail-policy half of the same class (T-01KZW2DQKN5C1BANMMTTMPK8TS / PR #490); raised by `adversarial-review --provider codex` on that branch. Deliberately NOT fixed there: that ticket's declared scope excludes the deny-set, and the two guards are intentionally decoupled — the deny-set is always-on artifact protection while the rail check is per-ticket policy.

=== MEASURED ===

`handoffTargetsOf` (`plugins/adlc-opencode/lib/handoff-gate.mjs`) unions `extractTargets` with three TOP-LEVEL string keys, so every non-scalar spelling reaches `checkHandoff` with an empty `editRelPaths`:

| argument shape | opencode | pi |
|---|---|---|
| `{target: '.adlc/.deny-store'}` | seen | seen |
| `{edits: [{target: '.adlc/.deny-store'}]}` | **MISSED** | **MISSED** |
| `{target: ['.adlc/.deny-store']}` | **MISSED** | seen |
| `{target: {path: '.adlc/.deny-store'}}` | **MISSED** | seen |
| `{batch: {nested: {target: '.adlc/.deny-store'}}}` | **MISSED** | not measured |

pi's `editTargetsOf` unions `extractToolPaths`, which recurses one level and matches a `target` key, so it covers more — but an object nested inside an ARRAY (`edits[]`) is still missed on both.

The Claude Code and Codex hooks collect edit paths payload-wide (`collectEditPaths`) and are believed unaffected; confirm rather than assume, and pin whatever is true.

=== WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN ON THE RAIL SIDE ===

The rail check has an unbypassable commit-time backstop: `scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs` re-derives the frozen set from the trusted base and rejects any PR that edits a rail, in any spelling. The deny-set has NO such backstop — `.adlc/*` is gitignored, so erasing a deny marker or the sentinel never reaches a diff. An in-session miss is the whole control.

Exploit shape: after a deny record is consumed, a fresh session is no longer denied wholesale. A third-party batch writer or deleter invoked with `{edits: [{target: '.adlc/handoffs/denies/<denier>.json'}]}` reaches `checkHandoff` with no protected path, is allowed, and erases the durable identity keeping the ORIGINAL denier sticky. Nothing downstream can notice.

=== REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR ===

1. Every harness that routes third-party tool arguments into the deny-set MUST recognize a protected artifact named through any of: a bare string, an array of strings, an object carrying a conventional path field, an object nested inside an array, and arbitrary further nesting. There is no depth at which the guard stops looking.
2. Extraction must NOT decay into a string scanner: a non-target key holding a path-shaped string (`{notes: ['.adlc/.deny-store']}`, `{description: 'delete .adlc/.deny-store'}`) must not be treated as a target, or ordinary tool calls start failing.
3. Termination is structural: self-referencing arguments must not hang the gate, and no numeric depth ceiling may be used — a ceiling is itself a bypass, since nesting one level past it stops the search. PR #490 uses an iterative walk with a seen-set for exactly this reason; reuse that shape.
4. The deny-set extractor stays INDEPENDENT of the rail extractor. They answer different questions and one must not be refactored to call the other; shared behaviour belongs in the package, not in a cross-import between a plugin's two gates.
5. The core D1-D3 semantics, band thresholds, and the frozen Claude Code contract are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An OpenCode custom tool naming a protected artifact via `{edits: [{target: ...}]}`, `{target: [...]}`, `{target: {path: ...}}`, or deeper nesting is denied at the real `tool.execute.before` entrypoint. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- The same shapes are denied through pi's real `tool_call` entrypoint. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-pi/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- Each shape proves it bites: against the pre-fix extractor it is ALLOWED, asserted against a fixture rather than by inspection. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs plugins/adlc-pi/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- A non-target key holding a path-shaped string is still allowed on a cold store, in both harnesses. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs plugins/adlc-pi/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- Self-referencing tool arguments terminate rather than hanging, asserted by a test that completes. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-opencode/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- The Claude Code and Codex payload-wide collectors are confirmed against the same shape matrix, and whatever holds is pinned by a test. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-secret-scrub.test.mjs plugins/adlc-codex/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- No numeric depth ceiling appears in any deny-set extractor. verify: `rg -n 'depth\s*[<>]=?\s*[0-9]' plugins/adlc-opencode/lib plugins/adlc-pi/lib packages/context-handoff/lib`
- The frozen Claude Code handoff contract and the package D1-D3 suites pass unmodified. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs packages/context-handoff/test/*.test.mjs && git diff --quiet origin/main -- plugins/adlc-claude-code/hooks/test/handoff-deny.test.mjs`
- The integrations pages state which argument shapes the deny-set can see and that it has no CI backstop. verify: `rg -q 'no CI backstop|not.*backstop' apps/docs/content/docs/integrations/opencode.mdx apps/docs/content/docs/integrations/pi.mdx`
- The three CI gates pass on a freshly fetched base. verify: `npm run preflight`
- Trust-root tier: a distinct-provider cross-model approve is recorded before merge. verify: `node packages/prosecute/bin/adlc-prosecute.mjs tier-check --base origin/main --author-provider anthropic`

allow-suppression: none

=== RAILS NOTE ===

The two handoff-gate modules and their harness test files are deliberately NOT railed: all four must change. Frozen here are the Claude Code contract and the package D1-D3 suites, which requirement 5 says must not move.

Out of scope: the rail-policy extractor (`extractTargets` / `spoofCandidateTargets`, fixed in T-01KZW2DQKN5C1BANMMTTMPK8TS); moving deny state to host-owned storage (T-01KZRCNX3TSJ4C0PXZ28C9CB5N — that fix would make this one moot for the erase case, but not for the overwrite case, and neither blocks the other); the resolver trust root (T-01KZPRW2TBKCV66AZ00KYV6603); changing D1-D3 semantics or band thresholds.
title: context-handoff: the deny-set must see target arguments in every shape they arrive in
